result.title: PROVE: Probabilistic Visual Grounding via Patch-Level Evidence for Vision-Language Models
result.summary: Visual grounding with vision-language models such as CLIP typically produces a single deterministic relevance map for an image-query pair, without indicating whether the localisation is reliable or whether the referent is present at all. We introduce \textbf{PROVE} (\textbf{Pro}babilistic \textbf{V}isual Grounding via Patch-Level \textbf{E}vidence), a post-hoc evidential adapter that maps frozen CLIP patch features to per-patch Beta distributions without modifying the backbone. PROVE casts grounding as per-patch membership: each patch accumulates positive and negative evidence for whether it belongs to the referent, so a query may match zero, one, or many patches. We train PROVE with an evidential objective on soft patch-coverage targets, and define a prior-pull objective that keeps absent-referent examples near an uninformative prior, so that vacuity serves as an absence signal without a dedicated presence classifier. During inference, a single forward pass yields, in closed form, a posterior-mean grounding map, a spatial vacuity map, and an image-level absence score. We evaluate PROVE on referring-expression benchmarks: it is competitive in localisation with state-of-the-art CLIP grounding methods, its uncertainty tracks localisation error and supports selective prediction under abstention, and its image-level score detects when the referent is absent altogether. Our evidential patch-membership modelling offers a simple, drop-in mechanism for probabilistic verification in frozen vision-language grounding systems.

AI.brief_summary: PROVE 提出冻结 CLIP 的事后证据适配器，将 patch 特征映射为每个 patch 的 Beta 分布，以正负证据累积建模 patch 是否属于指代对象；单次前向即给出定位图、空间 vacuity 图与图像级缺失分数。
AI.relevance_reason: 其 patch 级证据累积、vacuity 缺失信号与弃答下的选择性预测，可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与「何时停止/弃答」的依据；但方法面向定位而非推理期 latent 状态生成，迁移价值需进一步确认。
